body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),\quad \mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\)

sampling_model.design: Deterministic absorbing staggered adoption with the untreated cells missing by a nested staircase after each unit's adoption date.
sampling_model.units: A complete triangular array of deterministic low-rank mean panels with common regularity constants, fixed vanishing finite-slice rate envelopes, and jointly independent centered sub-Gaussian errors on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\). Variances are time-invariant within units but may differ across units, and both \(N_n\) and \(T_n\) may grow.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal effect is added after \(G_i\); the target averages eligible treated units with unit-share rather than equal-cohort weights.
sampling_model.overlap: Every eligible cohort-horizon block has donor-row and pre-period Gram eigenvalues bounded uniformly away from zero after size normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed feasible implementation uses exact blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals on \(\mathcal V_n\), unit-level residual variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\).  The oracle variance component is uniformly concentrated, while the imputation contamination and the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) loading discrepancy remain explicit diagnostics through \(d_i\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact eventwise score and staircase covariance, with feasible coverage conditional on displayed diagnostics

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The multiplier bootstrap yields asymptotically valid simultaneous inference for staggered group-time treatment effects under conditional parallel trends.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 3 is a finite-error conditional analogue under low-rank MNAR completion

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The data-driven intervals estimate each missing panel entry and match an instance-wise Bayesian Cramer--Rao lower bound.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present result uses their setting only as an entrywise comparator and makes no efficiency claim

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The preprint gives heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for individual effects and general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under staggered adoption.

body.tldr: The eligible-cohort Choi--Yuan blocks aggregate exactly into one event-by-cell score, whose covariance contains every shared staircase cell.  What is currently proved is an exact influence identity, a deterministic Choi--Yuan remainder implication with an honest finite union bound in the source i.i.d. homoskedastic submodel, oracle unit-variance concentration, exact feasible-score stability, and a finite-error Gaussian-multiplier theorem.  Growing-curve coverage follows only along arrays for which both the simultaneous block-remainder failure probability and the feasible score-loading failure probability vanish at the displayed rates.  The frozen assumptions alone do not establish either probability limit.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR results provide one-block, entrywise, scalar, or fixed-functional inference, while staggered DiD results provide simultaneous paths under parallel trends.  No located result supplies a growing adoption-aligned Choi--Yuan block remainder theorem under unit heteroskedasticity together with the rowwise score-loading rate needed by the frozen plug-in covariance.
project_justification.niche: The useful intermediate object is a primitive-cell event score with an exact shared-cell covariance and a finite-error inference theorem that exposes, rather than assumes, the two missing simultaneous controls.
project_justification.fill: The note fixes eligible-unit weights, aggregates the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients algebraically, proves the full staircase covariance, concentrates the oracle unit variances, and bounds covariance, scale, and correlation errors deterministically by \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).  A sign-expanded Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato approximation, singular-covariance-safe Gaussian comparison, and Gaussian anti-concentration yield an explicit coverage bound containing \(P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}\), \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\), the Choi--Yuan remainder perturbation, and the score-stability terms.  This is an actionable conditional protocol, not an unconditional theorem over the entire frozen class.

body.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, Proposition A.4 on pages 35--36 of arXiv:2308.02364v1, provide a one-block entrywise expansion under i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise with failure probability of order \(\min\{N_o^{-9},T_o^{-9}\}\).  Aggregating that result over a growing collection of eligible blocks yields only the finite union bound displayed here; their Supplement G.2 does not supply a growing-block theorem.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, Theorem 3.1 and Theorem C.2, analyze a fixed group functional under additional conditions and do not control the frozen leave-one-cell-out contamination or a growing rowwise score-loading error.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.1, and Lemma 3.1, supply the high-dimensional Gaussian approximation and covariance comparison used in the finite-error theorem without requiring nonsingular correlation.  Their confidence-band paper, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands}, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, supplies the anti-concentration step.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate event-time aggregation and the right-to-carry application, but do not establish the missing feasible growing-path rates.  Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, give simultaneous staggered paths under conditional parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion.  Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, and Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, provide entrywise or scalar low-rank inference, not this growing event-curve transfer.
body.interpretation: For an empirical right-to-carry event curve, the common critical value is conditionally calibrated once the realized score discrepancy is small and a simultaneous block-remainder guarantee is justified.  The exact covariance formula prevents treating reused donor or pre-treatment cells as independent, but it does not by itself certify the plug-in covariance.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen Choi--Yuan ratios control a published one-block perturbation expression, not a simultaneous heterogeneous block event.  The direct source union bound need not vanish as the number of cohort-horizon blocks grows.  Separately, variance replication concentrates \(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\), but no frozen premise controls \(\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it}\) or the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) error of \(\widehat c\).  Therefore neither \(\|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) nor \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}(\log^{-2}(2K))\) is claimed over the full class.  The attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remains open, and the balanced rank-one diagnostic gives no converse for the coarse published envelope.
body.honest_scope: The target is the eligible-cohort unit-share event curve for a deterministic adoption schedule under exact low rank, donor and pre-period Gram overlap, and independent centered row-heteroskedastic sub-Gaussian cell noise.  The settled results are the exact eventwise score and staircase covariance identities, together with a finite-error feasible-inference bound that displays the simultaneous remainder and score-loading failure probabilities.  Asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) coverage is asserted only on subclasses or individual arrays where those probabilities vanish and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\).  Serial dependence, approximate rank, tuning selection, the two growing-block rates, and the attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remain open.
